t.E553b.agn: In 2018, EFSA saw no indication of genotoxicity or developmental toxicity for calcium and magnesium silicate and talc; however, noting that accumulation of silicon from calcium silicate in the kidney and liver of rats had been reported and that there were no reliable long-term toxicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive data, it concluded that their safety as additives could not be assessed. It stated that the group ADI set by the SCF in 1991 for silicon dioxide and silicates was no longer valid. In 1986, JECFA had set the ADI as 'not specified'. In 2025, IARC classified talc in Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans) (Monograph 136).
t.E553b.eff.0.t: EFSA could not assess its safety because there are no reliable long-term toxicity, carcinogenicity and reproductive data
t.E553b.eff.1.t: In 2025, IARC classified talc in Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans)
t.E553b.eval: In 2025, IARC classified talc in Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans) (Monograph 136). In 2018, EFSA could not assess its safety as an additive because long-term toxicity data were lacking. In the EU it is permitted as an anti-caking agent on the surface of rice, sausages and boiled eggs, in chewing gum and in powdered foods.
t.E553b.found.2: Surface of unpeeled coloured boiled eggs (up to 5,400 mg/kg)
t.E553b.found.4: Powdered foods, sliced or grated cheese, foods in tablet form and food supplements (E 551–553 group)
t.E553b.prod: It is a natural clay or mineral (purified).
t.E553b.regx.0: Re-evaluated; safety could not be assessed due to lack of data; the SCF group ADI was considered no longer valid.
t.E553b.regx.1: Permitted at specified levels in powdered and tablet-form foods, cheese, salt, seasonings, chewing gum surfaces and food supplements (E 551–553 group).
t.E553b.summary: Talc, a natural mineral. Used as an anti-caking agent and on the surface of some confectionery.
t.E553b.what: It is talc, a natural magnesium silicate mineral; it prevents caking and is used for surface treatment.
